questions.stem: The third day of the four-day Pongal festival — specifically dedicated to cattle and livestock — is called:

options.option_text: Bhogi Pongal — observed on the eve of the main festival day
Surya Pongal — the principal day of offering to the Sun god
Mattu Pongal — when cows and bulls are bathed and adorned
Kanum Pongal — a day set aside for family visits and outings

questions.explanation: Mattu Pongal (day 3) honours cattle for their role in farming — cows and bulls are decorated and fed sweet pongal. Bhogi (day 1) involves discarding old items; Surya Pongal (day 2) is the main harvest-offering day to the Sun; Kanum Pongal (day 4) is reserved for family reunions and outings.

questions.stem: The word 'Chhath' in 'Chhath Puja' is derived from a numeral in Hindi/Bhojpuri, indicating the lunar tithi on which the festival's central rituals fall. Which numeral does it represent?

options.option_text: Four — the festival aligns with Chaturthi in Kartik Shukla Paksha
Five — the preparatory rituals begin on Panchami of Kartik month
Six — the sunset arghya falls on Shashti of Kartik Shukla Paksha
Seven — the post-sunrise arghya is offered on Saptami tithi

questions.explanation: 'Chhath' means six in Bhojpuri/Hindi; the core ritual of sunset arghya occurs on Kartik Shukla Shashti (sixth day), hence the festival is also called 'Surya Shashti'. Option D is the classic trap — while the post-sunrise arghya does fall on Saptami, the festival is named after Shashti when the central vrat reaches its peak.

questions.stem: Thrissur Pooram — acclaimed as the 'festival of festivals' in Kerala — is centred on which temple located in the heart of Thrissur city?

options.option_text: Guruvayur Sri Krishna Temple, a celebrated Vaishnava shrine nearby
Vadakkumnathan Temple, the ancient Shiva shrine at Thrissur's core
Sree Poornathrayeesa Temple situated at Tripunithura in Ernakulam
Paramekkavu Bhagavati Temple, one of the two procession participants

questions.explanation: Vadakkumnathan (Lord Shiva) Temple is the presiding shrine of Thrissur Pooram; the famous elephant procession and 'kudamattam' (parasol exchange) take place on its grounds. Guruvayur is the most common distractor — it is a celebrated temple in the same district but hosts a separate festival. Paramekkavu is one of two participant temples, not the central shrine.

questions.stem: The Pushkar Mela in Rajasthan is held beside a sacred lake associated with one of India's rarest temples — the only widely recognised one dedicated to which deity?

options.option_text: Lord Shiva — the most widely worshipped deity across Indian temples
Lord Brahma — very few prominent temples are dedicated to him
Lord Vishnu — extensively venerated within the Pushkar sacred complex
Goddess Saraswati — consort of Brahma, also venerated at Pushkar

questions.explanation: The Brahma Temple at Pushkar is one of the very few temples in India dedicated to Lord Brahma; folklore attributes this scarcity to a curse by Savitri after he performed a yagna with Gayatri. Saraswati is the classic trap — she too has a temple at Pushkar, but the landmark designation belongs to the Brahma temple.

questions.stem: The 'Chapchar Kut' spring festival of Mizoram is traditionally celebrated to mark the completion of which agricultural activity preceding the main sowing season?

options.option_text: Completion of paddy transplantation into the terrace field plots
Conclusion of the rice-harvesting season in late December
Completion of jungle clearing (jhum) in preparation for sowing
Beginning of the rabi crop cycle during the cool winter months

questions.explanation: Chapchar Kut (February–March) celebrates the community's collective completion of the hardest phase of jhum (shifting) cultivation — clearing the jungle — before the fields are burned and seeds sown. Options A and B are later and earlier stages of the agrarian cycle respectively, not the event that triggers this festival.

questions.stem: 'Theyyam' — the ritualistic performance art of Kerala in which artists embody deities — is predominantly practised in which geographical region of the state?

options.option_text: Ernakulam and Thrissur — the central and commercial belt of Kerala
Wayanad and Idukki — the eastern highland and tribal hill districts
Thiruvananthapuram and Kollam — the southernmost coastal districts
Kannur and Kasaragod — the northern Malabar region of Kerala

questions.explanation: Theyyam is the living ritual tradition of the northern Malabar belt (Kannur and Kasaragod), rooted in the folk-deity worship of Kolathunadu, where it is performed by specific caste groups in family shrines (kaavus). Thrissur (associated with Pooram) and Wayanad (tribal Adivasi festivals) are common distractors but are not the geographic home of Theyyam.

questions.stem: The 'Nongkrem Dance' — a five-day annual thanksgiving festival held at Smit village in the East Khasi Hills — belongs to which indigenous community of Meghalaya?

options.option_text: Garo community — who celebrate the analogous Wangala harvest festival
Jaintia community — known for the Behdienkhlam festival at Jowai
Khasi community — virgins perform Ka Shad Nongkrem at Smit village
Bodo community of Assam — who observe the Bwisagu spring festival

questions.explanation: Nongkrem is the most important festival of the Khasi people, performed at Smit (traditional capital of the Khyrim Syiemship) in East Khasi Hills; unmarried girls perform Ka Shad Nongkrem while men perform Ki Shad Mastieh. Options A and B (Wangala-Garo; Behdienkhlam-Jaintia) are the high-profile analogous festivals of the other two major Meghalayan tribes — a classic three-option trap set by examiners.
